fixed.what: One defect, found already fixed from the interrupted run and checked against the current code. applyLadderToPreset no longer takes Clear HDR from the camera. It sanitises the Favorite twice, as SDR and as Clear HDR. The Clear HDR reading counts only when it keeps the Favorite's size and either keeps its bits or is the 16-bit mode. The Favorite loads when a reading that keeps it matches what the ladder runs at its FPS, otherwise it is refused. The refusal message names the Favorite by that reading, SDR when both readings keep it. Traced cases: on Resolution 1 a 4K 12-bit 50 fps Favorite loads on Resolution 2, and on Resolution 2 a 16-bit 24 fps Favorite loads on Resolution 1. A 2K binned SDR Favorite is never silently forced to 4K Clear HDR. A pre-ladder 4K SDR 12-bit Favorite at 24 fps is still refused against 4K Clear HDR 16-bit, as the spec says.

The extractor also copies ladderSizeOf and ladderCropOf.

fixed.what: InfoLine gets an opt-in property, subMaximumLineCount (default 1, so other InfoLines are unchanged). Above 1, the sub Text uses Text.Wrap with that maximumLineCount and ElideRight as the last resort, so it never draws outside its column. The row grows by the extra lines through a new subExtraHeight (lineCount-1 lines; 0 for one line). The FORMAT InfoLine is now id formatInfoLine with subMaximumLineCount 4. In every landscape layout the stats Column is vertically centred, so its verticalCenterOffset now subtracts formatInfoLine.subExtraHeight/2; the column then grows upward only and its bottom stays put. On a rung (ladderRung > 0), a new formatLadderSubtext turns the spaces inside each part of Core's running line into no-break spaces, so the line wraps only at ' · '. The off-ladder text 'Mode Ladder on · the next FPS pick chooses the resolution' keeps normal word wrap. I used 4 lines, not 2: measured with Inter and DejaVu, the full line does not fit in two lines of any column (square 154 px needs 4, compact 120 px at 9 px needs 3), so two lines would elide part of Core's text.
